entries.grounds: Mutant is as stated. mutant_view and the builder (validation.v2.mutation.mutants(src,'_stream_matches',enums)[29]) give desc EXACTLY 'L596 string "a regex shape is searched by the harness's bounded search: none was given" emptied'; the diff turns TypeError("...") into TypeError('') at the regex/search-is-None guard; the exception TYPE is unchanged and the branch is taken on the same input. Independently confirmed the three load-bearing claims. (1) Reachability: grep shows _stream_matches is called only at cli_invocation.py:662 inside cli_invocation's own verdict_of, and only when cls=='exits_streams'. The only two production callers of that verdict_of are _observe (1162-1166), which always binds a concrete `search` closure over search_in_worker via functools.partial, and verdict_of('equality',...) at 1192, which never reaches the regex branch. So search-is-None+regex is unreachable in production. (The draft's mention of file_artifact/python_callable/python_callable_v2/process_effect verdict_of callers is loose but harmless: those are entirely separate verdict_of functions in separate modules that never call _stream_matches at all.) (2) No reader of the message: grep of the message fragments ('none was given','bounded search','a regex shape is searched') across aisef2/validation/tests/docs finds it only at the source (596), an unrelated bundle_cli.py message, and a DOCSTRING paraphrase in test_c2_cli_verdicts.py:240 (not an assertion). F7 (test_c2_cli_verdicts.py:244-247) reaches the exact branch but uses assertRaises(TypeError) on the TYPE only. _Later.settle (1343-1348) catches StreamSearchFailed only; a TypeError propagates uncaught and the OBSERVED detail is json.dumps(_public(facts)), not the message. (3) Kill-file runs (snapshot 4ec961e, isolated env: PATH stripped of both opencode dirs, HOME/TMPDIR under my tree, PYTHONPATH=tree, python3 -P -B). I resolved the FULL registered set from V21_TARGETS = ['tests/v2/test_c2_cli_verdicts.py','tests/v2/test_v21_identity.py','tests/v2/test_v21_r5_regex_worker.py'] (the draft named only the last). All three PASS unmutated (20 / 13 / 34 tests OK; test_v21_identity needed closure-evidence/v2/release/LEDGERLOCK-PROJECT.json, which I supplied via git show) and all three PASS on the mutant (20 / 13 / 34 OK). None kills it. Survivor confirmed; AUDITED stands.

exceptions_checked: Owner rule 'a string read by an operator or a verifier is not harmless': does not apply -- verified the message never reaches an operator report or a review verifier (settle catches only StreamSearchFailed; detail is facts JSON; the branch itself is unreachable in a real run because observe always supplies a bounded search). It is a developer diagnostic for a missing-argument programmer error.

The contract that matters -- 'a regex shape without a search is a TypeError, not an unbounded re.search' -- is the TYPE, preserved by the mutant and pinned by test_c2_cli_verdicts.py F7 via assertRaises(TypeError).

Not EQUIVALENT: the mutant IS observably different on a search=None+regex call (TypeError('') vs the worded TypeError), so it is not provably indistinguishable; it is AUDITED because no reader depends on the wording and the branch cannot be reached in production.
No test owed: adding a message-text assertion would only pin wording no operator/verifier reads -- adding a test merely to reach a number, which the owner rule forbids.
